parties: Anil Kumar Jain; Indo Count Industries Limited
headline: Anil Kumar Jain files SEBI Regulation 31(4) substantial acquisition disclosure with NSE for Indo Count Industries
sum: Anil Kumar Jain has filed a mandatory substantial acquisition disclosure under SEBI Takeover Code Regulation 31(4) with NSE, triggering formal shareholding transparency obligations and potential open offer / defensive mechanics for Indo Count Industries Limited.
implication: Regulation 31(4) filing is a gating checkpoint: acquirer has 4 business days to decide on open offer (if ≥25% threshold crossed) or negotiate exemptions; triggers para-materiality reviews and potential delisting/preferential issue defences.
detail: Anil Kumar Jain submitted a formal Regulation 31(4) disclosure to NSE regarding a substantial acquisition of shares in Indo Count Industries Limited. Under the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, any acquisition crossing specified ownership thresholds mandates immediate disclosure of shareholding, acquisition mode and timing to both the exchange and target company. The filing indicates a material change in shareholding structure; specific consideration, share count and threshold crossed are not disclosed in the public header but must appear in the full disclosure document.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, Regulation 31(4)
framework.note: Mandatory disclosure requirement within 2 business days of acquisition crossing 5% or further incremental thresholds.
Defines 'acquisition of shares' and applies presumption of concert where coordinated parties operate together.

framework.ref: SEBI Takeover Code, Regulation 10 and Schedule I
framework.note: Threshold calculation (5%, 10%, 15%, 25%, etc.) and para-materiality rules; open offer trigger at 25% if no exemption.
Open offer obligation triggered if threshold crossed; acquirer must make general offer to remaining shareholders within 4 business days or seek exemption.
Preferential allotment provisions; target may counter-acquire or issue shares as defensive mechanism post-disclosure.

framework.ref: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, Regulation 30
framework.note: Continuous disclosure requirement for material developments; company must announce receipt of Regulation 31(4) filing.
Exemptions from open offer for certain categories (employee trusts, institutional investors) may apply depending on acquirer profile.
Capital gains tax treatment of acquisition; varies by acquirer domicile and holding period post-acquisition.

conditions: Mandatory disclosure filed under Regulation 31(4) within 2 business days of acquisition
NSE and BSE announcement required simultaneously
Target company (ICIL) must be informed of shareholding and acquisition mode
Acquirer decision on open offer within 4 business days if threshold ≥25% and no exemption claimed
approvals: SEBI clearance not required for disclosure itself (mandatory filing); open offer approval by stock exchange if triggered
structure.novel: Standard Regulation 31(4) filing; no novel structuring evident from disclosure header.

triggers.note: Triggers on crossing specified shareholding thresholds (5%, 10%, 15%, 25%, etc.); disclosure due within 2 business days.
If Regulation 31(4) reveals ≥25% acquisition, open offer mandatory unless exemption (e.g., stock exchange approval for merger or FIPB waiver).
Target company must make immediate disclosure to exchanges upon receipt of Regulation 31(4) filing.
